title: Enhancing Shared Autonomy in Teleoperation under Network Delay: Transparency- and Confidence-Aware Arbitration
abstract: Shared autonomy framework where arbitration coefficient α is dynamically computed from dual confidence: autonomy confidence from TP-HSMM state covariances, and human confidence from teleoperation transparency under network delay. Integrates variable impedance control with three-port passivity guarantees.
relevance_to_vist: DIRECT COMPETITOR. Same continuous α arbitration idea, but principled (uncertainty-driven) vs VIST's heuristic. Uses haptic device transparency for human confidence — VIST uses exoskeleton without force feedback. Opportunity: visual confidence signal instead of haptic transparency.

title: SUBTA: A Framework for Supported User-Guided Bimanual Teleoperation in Structured Assembly
venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: GNN + dynamic self-attention predicts task label and bimanual actions from hand pose sequences. Scene graph with graph edit distance plans next target pose. 9 gated motion behaviors for execution. 12-person user study: position accuracy p<0.001, mental load p=0.002. Honda Research Institute.
relevance_to_vist: Addresses Reviewer 3's criticism: intent inference from observation (not known goal). Scene-graph-based target pose planning shows how to remove the 'known target pose' assumption.

title: A Model Predictive Control Approach to Blending in Shared Control
abstract: Reformulates shared-control blending as constrained optimal control with MPC. Guarantees feasibility, enforces safety constraints, anticipates limits over receding horizon. Related to Jabbour PhD thesis on dual-component adaptive assistance (AKF + MPC). INRIA Aucius team.
relevance_to_vist: Same technical lineage (AKF+MPC for shared control). Need to verify which parts are already published vs. still in thesis — unpublished parts = opportunity space.

title: Adaptor: Advancing Assistive Teleoperation with Few-Shot Learning and Cross-Operator Generalization
venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Two-stage few-shot intent learning: preprocessing models intent uncertainty via noise injection + geometry-aware keyframe extraction; policy stage fuses Intention Expert with VLM context via Conditional Flow Matching. +41.9% success rate, 83.2% novice success rate.
relevance_to_vist: Noise injection for intent uncertainty modeling is directly applicable to VIST L1 (Learning α from demonstration). Shows how to make learned α handle uncertainty.

title: RINSE: Learning from the Best: Smoothness-Driven Metrics for Data Quality in Imitation Learning
abstract: Lightweight policy-agnostic framework scoring demonstrations via SAL (Spectral Arc Length, frequency-domain) and TED (Trajectory-Envelope Distance, spatial). SAL filtering: 16% higher success using 1/6 data on RoboMimic. UCLA.
relevance_to_vist: If VIST still claims 'physically-regularized demonstration data', must compare against RINSE's smoothness-driven filtering. Shows a principled data-quality baseline.

title: SAPS: Shared Autonomy for Policy Steering by Blending Teleoperation with a Pretrained VLA
abstract: Lightweight model-agnostic framework blending real-time human teleoperation with pretrained VLA actions. Three arbitration strategies including dynamic cosine-similarity blending. Boosts π0.5 from 15% to 92.6% success on LIBERO-PRO with 10.8-30% human intervention rate. CMU.
relevance_to_vist: Cosine similarity as arbitration signal — alternative to confidence-based approach. Shows VLA-based shared control landscape, which VIST should be aware of for positioning.
